questions.stem: What does 「私の家は五人家族です。」 mean?
options: There are five people in my family.
My house has five rooms in it.
Five families live in my building.
My family has lived here five years.
questions.explanation: 「五人家族」 describes a family of five people, so the sentence gives the size of the speaker's family. 「家」 here means the household, not the building, and nothing in the sentence refers to rooms or years.

questions.stem: How do you ask a classmate how many people are in her family?
options: 「家族はどこですか。」
「何年家族ですか。」
「何人家族ですか。」
「何の家族ですか。」
questions.explanation: 「何人家族ですか。」 asks 'How many people are in your family?', using the counter 「人」 for people. 「何の家族ですか。」 would ask what kind of family it is, and 「家族はどこですか。」 asks where the family is.

questions.stem: You are asking your friend Yui about her older brother. Which word do you use for him?
options: お兄さん
兄
弟さん
お姉さん
questions.explanation: Talking about someone else's family, you use the respectful term: 「お兄さん」 for an older brother. 「兄」 is the plain term for your own older brother, used when talking to people outside your family, so it would sound wrong for Yui's brother.

questions.stem: Which word is the polite way to refer to someone else's grandmother?
options: おかあさん
おばあさん
そぼ
おばさん
questions.explanation: 「おばあさん」 is the respectful word for another person's grandmother. 「そぼ」 is the humble word for your own grandmother, and 「おばさん」, with a short 「ば」, means aunt or a middle-aged woman.

questions.stem: What does 「いとこ」 mean?
options: uncle
cousin
aunt
nephew
questions.explanation: 「いとこ」 is a cousin, the child of an aunt or uncle. An aunt is 「おば」 (someone else's is 「おばさん」), an uncle is 「おじ」 and a nephew is 「おい」.

questions.stem: Read: 「平日、父は朝早く家を出て、夜おそく帰ります。だから、晩ごはんはたいてい母と私と弟の三人で食べます。」 Who usually eats dinner together on weekdays?
options: The writer, her father and her younger brother
Only the writer and her mother
The writer, her mother and her younger brother
The whole family, all four of them
questions.explanation: Her father leaves early and comes home late on weekdays (「平日」), so dinner is usually 「母と私と弟の三人」: three people. Her father is the one missing, which rules out the whole family and any group with him in it.

questions.stem: Read: 「むかしの日本では、『おとこは外ではたらき、おんなは家をまもる』という考え方がふつうでした。今は、家事や子そだてをするお父さんもふえています。」 What change does the passage describe?
options: Men and women have always shared the work
More fathers now do housework and raise children
Fewer mothers now work outside the home
Most fathers now stay at home full-time
questions.explanation: The passage contrasts an old view (men work outside, women look after the home) with today, when more fathers (「お父さんもふえています」) do housework and child-raising. It says more fathers are involved, not that most stay home, and it presents the old view as having changed.

questions.stem: What is a 「せんぎょうしゅふ」?
options: A woman who runs a family business
A woman whose full-time role is running the home
A mother who works part-time in a shop
A grandmother who lives with the family
questions.explanation: 「せんぎょうしゅふ」 is a full-time homemaker, a role that matched the stereotype of the post-war Japanese family. A mother with a part-time job is usually said to work 「パート」, which is a different arrangement.

questions.stem: What does the word 「イクメン」 describe?
options: A young man who still lives at home with his parents
A man who works very long hours at a company
A boy who looks after his younger siblings
A father who takes an active part in raising his children
questions.explanation: 「イクメン」 joins 「いくじ」 (raising children) with 'men' and names a father who is closely involved in childcare. The word spread because it challenged the stereotype of the father who is rarely at home.

questions.stem: Which word completes 「私の家族も、ゆいさんの家族と ___ 四人家族です。」 ('My family is also a family of four, the same as Yui's')?
options: 同じ
同じな
同じの
同じに
questions.explanation: 「同じ」 goes straight before a noun with nothing added: 「同じ四人家族」, 「同じクラス」. Although it behaves like a な-adjective elsewhere (「同じだ」), it never takes 「な」 or 「の」 before a noun, and 「同じに」 would be adverbial.

questions.stem: What does 「私は母にかおがにています。」 mean?
options: My mother looks younger than I do.
I see my mother's face every day.
My face looks like my mother's.
My mother does my make-up for me.
questions.explanation: 「〜ににている」 means 'to resemble' and is used in the ている form for a lasting likeness. 「かおが」 narrows it to the face: I take after my mother in looks. Nothing in the sentence compares ages.

questions.stem: What does 「お正月には、いつもいなかのそふぼの家に行きます。」 mean?
options: At New Year we always go to my grandparents' place in the country.
At New Year my grandparents always come to our house in the city.
At New Year we sometimes visit my grandparents' new home in town.
At New Year my grandparents always go to the country on holiday.
questions.explanation: 「いなかのそふぼの家」 is my grandparents' house in the country, and 「いつも〜行きます」 says we always go there. Visiting grandparents in a home town at New Year or おぼん is a common way Japanese families keep in touch with extended family.

questions.stem: Read: 「そふぼは北海道に住んでいるので、あまり会えません。でも、毎週日曜日にビデオ電話で話しています。」 How does the writer stay connected with her grandparents?
options: By visiting them every Sunday
By writing to them every week
By living in the same house
By video call every Sunday
questions.explanation: Her grandparents live in Hokkaido, so she can rarely see them (「あまり会えません」), but they talk by video call (「ビデオ電話」) every Sunday. The sentence rules out regular visits, and they clearly do not live together.

questions.stem: What does 「友達とプリクラをとりました。」 mean?
options: I took photo-booth sticker pictures with my friends.
I had my photo taken by my friends at school.
I bought some printed stickers for my friends.
I made a photo album to give to my friends.
questions.explanation: 「プリクラ」 are photo booths that print decorated sticker pictures, popular with Japanese teenagers as something to do with friends. 「とる」 is the verb for taking a photo, and 「友達と」 means with friends.

questions.stem: Which messaging app do young people in Japan most widely use to keep in touch with friends?
options: LINE
WhatsApp
WeChat
Telegram
questions.explanation: LINE is by far the most used messaging app in Japan, and class and club groups often run on it. WhatsApp is widely used in Australia and many other countries but is far less common among Japanese teenagers.

questions.stem: In talk about messaging between friends, what does 「きどくスルー」 mean?
options: Deleting a message before reading it
Forwarding a message on to other people
Replying to a message with only a sticker
Reading a message and not replying to it
questions.explanation: 「きどく」 is the 'read' mark the sender sees, and 「スルー」 (from 'through') means letting something pass. Seeing that a friend has read a message but not answered can cause hurt feelings, one of the challenges of keeping friendships online.

questions.stem: What does 「気があう」 mean in 「ゆきさんとは気があうので、すぐ友達になりました。」?
options: We argue a lot
We are in the same class
We feel nervous together
We get along naturally
questions.explanation: 「気があう」 means two people get on well because they think and feel alike, so the speaker and Yuki became friends quickly. Arguing would be 「けんかする」, and being in the same class would be 「同じクラス」.

questions.stem: What does 「なかまはずれにされる」 mean?
options: To leave a group of your own accord
To be praised by your whole group
To be left out of a group
To be chosen as a group leader
questions.explanation: 「なかま」 is a group of companions and 「はずれ」 means being outside it; 「される」 makes it something done to you. Being left out is one of the challenges young people face in friendships, unlike choosing to leave, which would be 「やめる」 or 「ぬける」.

questions.stem: Which sentence invites a new classmate to eat lunch with you?
options: 「いっしょにおべんとうを食べませんか。」
「いっしょにおべんとうを食べましたか。」
「いっしょにおべんとうを食べたいですか。」
「いっしょにおべんとうを食べてください。」
questions.explanation: A negative question, 「〜ませんか」, is the usual polite invitation: 'Won't you eat with me?' 「食べましたか」 asks about the past, and asking someone 「食べたいですか」 directly about their wants sounds blunt as an invitation.

questions.stem: Which verb completes 「クラブに入ると、すぐ友達が ___。」 ('If you join a club, you soon make friends')?
options: します
できます
作ります
なります
questions.explanation: 'To make friends' is 「友達ができる」, with 「が」 marking the friends who come into being. 「友達が作ります」 would make the friends the ones doing the making, and 「なります」 needs a complement such as 「友達になります」.

questions.stem: Read: 「新しい学校に入った時、友達ができるかどうか、とてもしんぱいでした。」 What was the writer worried about?
options: Whether she would make any friends
Whether her friends would change schools
Whether she could find the new school
Whether her old friends would forget her
questions.explanation: 「友達ができるかどうか」 means 'whether or not I would make friends', and 「しんぱいでした」 says she was worried about it when she started at the new school. Nothing in the sentence mentions her old friends.

questions.stem: Read the text message: 「ごめん、きのうはいそがしくて、へんじできなかった。おこってる？」 What is the writer doing?
options: Saying she is angry that her friend didn't reply
Explaining that she is too busy to meet today
Asking her friend why she was so busy yesterday
Apologising for not replying and checking her friend isn't angry
questions.explanation: 「ごめん」 apologises, 「へんじできなかった」 says she could not reply yesterday, and 「おこってる？」 asks whether her friend is angry. It is the writer who failed to reply, so she is not the one who is annoyed.

questions.stem: Read: 「ケンとは小学校からの友達だ。中学で同じクラスにならなかった時は、少しさびしかった。でも、毎日いっしょに帰ったので、今も友達だ。」 What kept the friendship going?
options: They sent each other messages every night
They walked home together every day
They were always in the same class
They joined the same club in high school
questions.explanation: When they were put in different classes at junior high, the writer felt a little lonely, but they went home together every day (「毎日いっしょに帰った」), so they are still friends. The passage says they were not in the same class at junior high.

questions.stem: You are discussing a story about two friends. Which sentence gives your personal opinion of their relationship?
options: 「私は、二人はほんとうにいい友達だと思います。」
「二人は同じ町に住んでいて、同じ学校に行っています。」
「話の中で、二人は夏休みにいっしょに海に行きます。」
「二人は小学校の時に、はじめて会いました。」
questions.explanation: 「私は〜と思います」 marks an opinion, and 「ほんとうにいい友達」 is a judgement about the relationship. The other sentences report events and details from the story, which can be checked against the text rather than argued.

questions.stem: A Japanese classmate says 「日本語がじょうずですね。」 Which reply is the modest response Japanese speakers expect?
options: 「いいえ、じょうずですよ。」
「いいえ、まだまだです。」
「はい、とてもじょうずです。」
「ありがとう、そうですね。」
questions.explanation: Accepting praise outright can sound boastful, so the usual reply plays it down: 「いいえ、まだまだです。」 ('No, I still have a long way to go'). Agreeing that you are very good, or confirming it with 「そうですね」, goes against this convention.

questions.stem: In which month does the school year begin in Japan?
options: January
April
February
September
questions.explanation: The Japanese school year begins in April, with entrance ceremonies as the cherry blossoms flower, and ends in March. In Australia the school year begins in late January or early February.

questions.stem: What is a 「入学式」?
options: A meeting where parents choose a school
A party held at the end of the school year
A ceremony welcoming new students to a school
An examination taken to enter a school
questions.explanation: 「入学」 means entering a school and 「式」 means ceremony, so 「入学式」 is the entrance ceremony held for new students, usually in early April. An entrance examination is a different thing, 「にゅうがくしけん」.

questions.stem: In many Japanese schools, who cleans the classrooms each day?
options: The students, at a set cleaning time
Paid cleaners, after the students go home
The teachers, before classes begin
Parent volunteers, once a week
questions.explanation: In most Japanese schools students clean their own classrooms, corridors and toilets during 「そうじ」 time, seen as teaching responsibility and care for shared spaces. In most Australian schools, paid cleaners do this after hours.

questions.stem: What are 「うわばき」 in a Japanese school?
options: School bags carried on the back
Indoor shoes worn inside the school
Sports shoes worn for physical education
Slippers kept for visiting parents
questions.explanation: Students change from outdoor shoes into 「うわばき」 at the shoe lockers by the entrance and wear them inside the building, as people take off outdoor shoes at home. Slippers for visitors are 「スリッパ」.

questions.stem: What is 「きゅうしょく」?
options: School lunch, eaten together in class
Lunch bought from a shop near the school
A packed lunch made at home each morning
A snack eaten after club activities
questions.explanation: 「きゅうしょく」 is school lunch, provided in most Japanese primary and junior high schools; students often serve it themselves and eat together in the classroom. A packed lunch from home is an 「おべんとう」, which many high school students bring.

questions.stem: What is 「ぶかつ」?
options: Homework set over the summer holidays
Part-time work done after school
School clubs such as sport or music
Extra lessons at a private study centre
questions.explanation: 「ぶかつ」 is short for club activities run by the school, from baseball and kendo to brass band and art, often meeting after school and on weekends. Private study centres are 「じゅく」 and part-time work is 「アルバイト」.

questions.stem: In a Japanese school, what is the 「たんにん」 teacher?
options: A teacher who replaces someone who is away
The teacher in charge of one class all year
The teacher who runs the school as principal
The teacher who coaches a sports club
questions.explanation: The 「たんにん」 looks after one class: taking the roll, passing on notices and guiding students through the year. The principal is the 「校長先生」, and the teacher who runs a club is its 「こもん」.

questions.stem: In a Japanese class, what does the student who is 「にっちょく」 do?
options: Represents the class on the student council
Leads the school team in sport for the term
Helps the teacher mark tests for the week
Takes a turn doing class duties for the day
questions.explanation: 「にっちょく」 is a duty that rotates through the class day by day: wiping the board, calling the class to stand and bow, and writing the class diary. Student council members are elected and serve much longer.

questions.stem: How many years of school are compulsory in Japan, and which schools do they cover?
options: Primary to senior high school, twelve years
Junior and senior high school, six years
Primary and junior high school, nine years
Primary school only, six years
questions.explanation: Compulsory education in Japan is six years of primary school (「小学校」) and three of junior high (「中学校」). Senior high school is not compulsory, though almost all students go on to it, usually after sitting an entrance examination.

questions.stem: Read: 「日本の中学生の多くは、こうこうに入るために、三年生の時にしけんをうけます。」 What does the sentence say?
options: Most high schools take students without an exam
Students sit an exam to finish their third year
Many students leave school after junior high
Many junior high students sit an exam to enter high school
questions.explanation: 「こうこうに入るために」 means 'in order to enter high school', and 「しけんをうけます」 means they sit an exam, which happens in the third year of junior high. Entrance exams make that year a stressful one for many students.

questions.stem: Read: 「オーストラリアの学校は一年に四つのがっきがありますが、日本の学校の多くは三つです。日本の夏休みは七月の終わりから八月までです。」 Which statement matches the passage?
options: Australian schools have three terms and a break in July-August
Japanese and Australian schools have the same number of terms
Many Japanese schools have three terms and a summer break in July-August
Japanese schools have four terms and a long break at Christmas
questions.explanation: The passage says Australian schools have four terms (「四つのがっき」) while many Japanese schools have three, and the Japanese summer holiday runs from late July into August. Australia's long break falls over December and January, its own summer.

questions.stem: Read: 「せいふくは、毎朝何を着るかえらばなくていいから楽です。でも、夏はあつくて、ちょっと大変です。」 What is the writer's view of school uniforms?
options: They should be replaced with free dress
They are expensive to buy every year
They are convenient, but uncomfortable in summer
They are uncomfortable all year round
questions.explanation: The writer gives a benefit (no need to choose clothes each morning, so it is easy) and a challenge (hot in summer). 「でも」 turns from one to the other; the writer never suggests getting rid of uniforms or mentions cost.

questions.stem: Read: 「ぶかつは毎日あって、しゅくだいをする時間があまりありません。でも、友達とがんばるのは楽しいです。」 How does the writer weigh up club activities?
options: Costly in study time, but fun with friends
Enjoyable, and they leave plenty of time for homework
So demanding that the writer plans to quit
Less important than homework and study
questions.explanation: The writer names a challenge (clubs every day leave little time for homework) and then, after 「でも」, a benefit: working hard with friends is fun. The passage gives no sign that the writer means to give the club up.
